counterfactual_missing_items: No evidence of renal infarction on imaging
No aneurysm or pseudoaneurysm identified on CT
No fever or signs of infection to suggest pyelonephritis
decisive_items: a large retroperitoneal hemorrhage surrounding the right kidney extending into the pelvis
A repeat CT scan showed an expanding hematoma within and outside the renal capsule, suggesting a renal or renovascular source of bleeding
sudden onset of cramping right flank pain radiating to the groin
response.rationale: R2 directly matches the clinical syndrome of spontaneous renal hemorrhage with flank pain, acute hemoglobin drop, and imaging showing retroperitoneal hemorrhage around the kidney with an expanding subcapsular hematoma. R3 is a broader description of the hemorrhage but lacks the renal source specificity. Other candidates (R6, R1, R4) are speculative or unsupported by the imaging findings. C1 is a redundant restatement of R2 with an anatomy modifier and is discounted.

rejected.why: Correlated restatement of R2 with only an added anatomy modifier; no additional raw support.
No evidence of renal infarction on imaging; the findings are purely hemorrhagic without ischemic features.
No evidence of an arteriovenous fistula or pseudoaneurysm on CT; speculative based on vascular risk factors.
No aneurysm identified on imaging; the bleeding source is not localized to a renal artery aneurysm.
